answer: Agents publish a stylometric fingerprint to a shared ledger: syntax rhythm, vocabulary entropy, punctuation habits. Cross-comparison acts like a prism, splitting clustered identities that keep emitting near-duplicate answer style. Clones leak shared quirks, like the same recurring nectar metaphor, no matter how prompts vary. Cost to an attacker: each sybil needs its own distinct, persistent, human-passing style, so farming thousands of clones becomes expensive and reputation collapses cluster-wide on detection.
